item.title: - Venerable Sir, the Blessed One does not enable me to attain the superhuman states of psychic power. - Sunakkhatta, did I say to you:…
item.description:
- Venerable Sir, the Blessed One does not enable me to attain the superhuman states of psychic power. - Sunakkhatta, did I say to you: 'Come, Sunakkhatta, live under my guidance! I will enable you to attain the superhuman states of psychic power'? - No, Venerable Sir. - Did you say to me: 'Venerable Sir, I will live under the guidance of the Blessed One, and the Blessed One will enable me to attain the superhuman states of psychic power'? - No, Venerable Sir. - Sunakkhatta, since I did not say to you, and you did not say to me, you foolish man, who are you and who am I that you speak of abandoning? Sunakkhatta, whether the superhuman states of psychic power are realized or not, the purpose for which I teach the Dhamma is to lead the practitioner to the complete destruction of suffering. Sunakkhatta, what then are the superhuman states of psychic power that need to be realized? See how great your transgression is, you foolish man!

From: Dīgha Nikāya 24 – Pāthikasutta

item.title: There is no entering upon the unwholesome, bhikkhus, as long as moral shame... moral dread... energy... wisdom are established in wholesome states. When moral shame...…
item.description:
There is no entering upon the unwholesome, bhikkhus, as long as moral shame... moral dread... energy... wisdom are established in wholesome states. When moral shame... moral dread... energy... wisdom disappear, bhikkhus, then shamelessness... fearlessness... laziness... evil wisdom arise and persist, then there is entering upon the unwholesome.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 5.6

item.title: Nigrodha, you are wise and senior, have you ever thought: 'The Buddha, the Enlightened One, teaches the Dhamma that leads to enlightenment; the Blessed One,…
item.description:
Nigrodha, you are wise and senior, have you ever thought: 'The Buddha, the Enlightened One, teaches the Dhamma that leads to enlightenment; the Blessed One, the Tamed One, teaches the Dhamma that leads to taming; the Blessed One, the Calmed One, teaches the Dhamma that leads to calming; the Blessed One, the One Gone to the Far Shore, teaches the Dhamma that leads to the far shore; the Blessed One, the One of Perfect Peace, teaches the Dhamma that leads to perfect peace.'

From: Dīgha Nikāya 25 – Udumbarika­sīhanādasutta

item.title: Ānanda, I have declared unequivocally that evil bodily action, evil verbal action, and evil mental action should not be done. If one does what should…
item.description:
Ānanda, I have declared unequivocally that evil bodily action, evil verbal action, and evil mental action should not be done. If one does what should not be done, the following dangers are to be expected: self-reproach; after being known, the wise reproach; a bad reputation spreads; one dies confused; and after death, with the breakup of the body, one is reborn in a plane of misery, a bad destination, a lower realm, hell. Therefore, Ānanda, I have declared unequivocally that evil bodily action, evil verbal action, and evil mental action should not be done. For one who does what should not be done, these are the dangers to be expected.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 2.18

item.title: Associate with a learned friend who upholds the Dhamma, A great-hearted, intelligent, and eloquent companion. Knowing the meaning, dispelling doubts, Live alone like a rhinoceros.…
item.description:
Associate with a learned friend who upholds the Dhamma,
A great-hearted, intelligent, and eloquent companion.
Knowing the meaning, dispelling doubts,
Live alone like a rhinoceros.

Not delighting in the pleasures of the world — song, dance, and sensual pleasures —
Wandering without adornment, without longing,
Uttering the truth, rejecting all ornament,
Live alone like a rhinoceros.

From: Sutta Nipāta 1.3

item.title: Bhikkhus, then the Bodhisatta Vipassī reflected: 'This consciousness turns back and forth, it does not go beyond name-and-form. Only to this extent one is born,…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, then the Bodhisatta Vipassī reflected: 'This consciousness turns back and forth, it does not go beyond name-and-form. Only to this extent one is born, or becomes old, or dies, or passes away, or is reborn, that is: conditioned by name-and-form, consciousness arises; conditioned by consciousness, name-and-form arises; conditioned by name-and-form, the six sense bases arise; conditioned by the six sense bases, contact arises; conditioned by contact, feeling arises; conditioned by feeling, craving arises; conditioned by craving, clinging arises; conditioned by clinging, existence arises; conditioned by existence, birth arises; conditioned by birth, aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair arise. Thus is the origination of this whole mass of suffering.'

From: Dīgha Nikāya 14 – Mahāpadānasutta

item.title: - Bhikkhus, there are these five kinds of stinginess. What five? Stinginess regarding dwellings, stinginess regarding families, stinginess regarding gains, stinginess regarding beauty, stinginess regarding…
item.description:
- Bhikkhus, there are these five kinds of stinginess. What five? Stinginess regarding dwellings, stinginess regarding families, stinginess regarding gains, stinginess regarding beauty, stinginess regarding Dhamma. Bhikkhus, for the abandonment of these five kinds of stinginess, the four establishments of mindfulness should be developed. What four? ... these four establishments of mindfulness should be developed.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 9.69

item.title: Bhikkhus, when dwelling thus with mindfulness established, the bhikkhu reflects on, examines, and investigates that Dhamma with wisdom, at that time the investigation-of-states enlightenment factor…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, when dwelling thus with mindfulness established, the bhikkhu reflects on, examines, and investigates that Dhamma with wisdom, at that time the investigation-of-states enlightenment factor is aroused in the bhikkhu. At that time, he develops the investigation-of-states enlightenment factor. At that time, the investigation-of-states enlightenment factor comes to fulfillment by development. When he reflects on, examines, and investigates that Dhamma with wisdom, unflagging energy is aroused in the bhikkhu. Bhikkhus, when the bhikkhu reflects on, examines, and investigates that Dhamma with wisdom, at that time unflagging energy is aroused in that bhikkhu. At that time, the energy enlightenment factor is aroused in the bhikkhu. At that time, he develops the energy enlightenment factor. At that time, the energy enlightenment factor comes to fulfillment by development. Non-material rapture arises in one who is energetic and striving.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 118 – Ānāpānassatisutta

item.title: Poverty and indebtedness Are called suffering in the world! A poor person in debt, Enjoying, is harmed, Then pursued by creditors, Even to being bound.…
item.description:
Poverty and indebtedness
Are called suffering in the world!
A poor person in debt,
Enjoying, is harmed,

Then pursued by creditors,
Even to being bound.
Being bound is indeed suffering
For one seeking sensual pleasures.

So too in the Noble Discipline,
Whoever lives without faith,
Without shame, without dread,
Decides on evil deeds.

Having done evil deeds
By body, speech, and mind,
And wishes: 'May no one know what I did.'

That person well conceals
With body, speech, and mind,
Increases evil deeds,
Here and there doing more.

An evil-witted, evil-deed person,
Knowing the evil he has done,
Like a poor person in debt,
Enjoying, is harmed.

Painful thoughts
Born from remorse
Still pursue that person,
In the village or in the forest.

An evil-deed, evil-witted person,
Knowing the evil he has done,
Either falls into the animal realm
Or is bound in hell.

This binding is suffering.
The wise are liberated.
One with serene mind who gives
With righteously gained goods,

Sowing good fortune on both paths,
A faithful householder seeking,
In the present obtains happiness,
In the hereafter obtains bliss.
Thus a householder's giving
Increases merit.

So too in the Noble Discipline
Faith is established.
With shame, with dread,
With wisdom, protecting virtue,

That one, in the Noble Discipline,
Is called 'one who dwells happily.'
He gains non-material happiness,
Established in equanimity.

Abandoning the five hindrances,
Always diligent, energetic,
Attains jhāna, one-pointed mind,
Careful, mindful.

Knowing that as it really is,
He destroys all fetters,
Without any clinging,
Rightly, his mind is liberated.

With that right liberation,
If such knowledge arises:
'Unshakable is my liberation,
The fetter of existence is destroyed.'

This knowledge is supreme knowledge,
This happiness is unsurpassed happiness,
Without sorrow, without defilement,
Secure, liberated.
This state of being free from debt
Is considered the highest.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.45

item.title: Just as, Sunakkhatta, a person who has not been living in his own village or town for a long time might see a person who…
item.description:
Just as, Sunakkhatta, a person who has not been living in his own village or town for a long time might see a person who has just arrived from that village or town. He would ask that person about the safety of that village or town, about the abundance of food and drink, and about the absence of disease; and that person would tell him about the safety, abundance, and good health. Sunakkhatta, what do you think? Would that person listen to him, lend an ear, and fix his mind on that knowledge, and would he associate with that person with delight?" — "Yes, Venerable Sir." — "So too, Sunakkhatta, this situation occurs when some people are heavily inclined towards material things. For one heavily inclined towards material things, Sunakkhatta, a talk that is suitable for him must be in accordance with his reflections and thoughts, and he will only associate with that person with delight. But if the talk is only about the imperturbable (āneñja), he will not listen, will not lend an ear, will not fix his mind on supreme knowledge, and will not associate with that person with delight. He should be understood as: 'A person heavily inclined towards material things.'

From: Majjhima Nikāya 105 – Sunakkhattasutta
